name: EPR (Efficient Prompt Retrieval) - Learning To Retrieve Prompts for In-Context Learning
venue: NAACL-HLT 2022 (Proceedings of the 2022 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies); preprint arXiv:2112.08633
authors_affiliation: Ohad Rubin, Jonathan Herzig, Jonathan Berant — The Blavatnik School of Computer Science, Tel Aviv University.
code_url: https://github.com/OhadRubin/EPR (author implementation; built on the DPR codebase; ~64 stars).
maintained_repo_url: N/A (single-paper author repo with a single initial commit Aug 2022; no continuously-updated leaderboard or paper list).
task_domain: In-context learning / few-shot demonstration (prompt) retrieval for structured NLP tasks; specifically semantic parsing (mapping natural-language utterances to meaning representations). QA-adjacent (sequence-to-sequence structured prediction).
problem_setting: Offline, supervised, single-model (no multi-agent) setting. Given a labeled training set D of input-output pairs and a scoring LM, the goal is to train a retriever R(x_test, D) that selects training examples (prompts) for a frozen inference LM that does in-context learning with no parameter updates. Supervision is available (gold y is used at training-data-construction time to retrieve high-quality candidates and to LM-score them). Two evaluation regimes: (a) LM-as-a-service (scoring LM == inference LM, e.g. both GPT-Neo, used as a black-box service) and (b) LM-as-a-proxy (small scoring LM, e.g. GPT-Neo, used to train a retriever later applied to larger inference LMs GPT-J/GPT-3/Codex). Retrieval is one-shot at test time; the retriever and index are frozen after offline training.
what_is_retrieved: Demonstrations (training input-output pairs / examples) used as in-context prompts. Each retrieved unit is a single labeled training example (utterance + meaning representation).
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus: the fixed annotated training set D is the retrieval store. It is not a growing/episodic agent memory; the index is built offline once and frozen.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Variable-size top-L ranking subject to a context budget: the retriever returns examples sorted by inner-product similarity, and the number actually used (L') is the largest set that fits in the inference LM's context window (C=2,048 tokens). Objective is similarity-style ranking (each candidate scored independently), not recovery of a minimal complete set; selection count is dynamic/budget-capped rather than a fixed k.
cbr_cycle_coverage: Retrieve (yes) / Reuse (yes, verbatim demonstrations injected into the prompt) / Revise (no) / Retain (no). Effectively [Retrieve, Reuse].
explicit_cbr_grounding: False as self-framing: EPR frames itself as prompt/demonstration retrieval, not case-based reasoning. However it explicitly includes a CASE-BASED REASONING (CBR) baseline adapted from Das et al. (2021) (KB-QA CBR), which it positions against. It does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner as its own framework.
retrieval_unit: Single demonstration (one training input-output pair: utterance + meaning representation). Granularity = single demo / case (problem-solution).
index_source: Static corpus, offline-induced: the annotated training set D is encoded offline with the trained prompt encoder E_P(.) and indexed with FAISS. No online/test-time growth.
index_structure_topology: Flat dense vector index (FAISS, maximum inner-product search over dense BERT-CLS embeddings of training examples).
retriever_type: Learned dense retriever (dual-encoder: input encoder E_X and prompt encoder E_P, both BERT-base, trained contrastively a la DPR). An unsupervised retriever (BM25 or SBERT) is used only to build the candidate set for training-data construction.
retriever_learning_signal: LM-feedback / contrastive on LM-scored labels. For each training example, candidate prompts are scored by the probability the scoring LM assigns to the gold output y given x and the candidate (s(e_l)=Prob_g_hat(y | e_l, x)); top-k candidates labeled positive, bottom-k labeled negative; a dense retriever is then trained with the DPR contrastive (in-batch negatives) objective. The signal is LM utility for decoding the target, argued to be a better proxy than surface-similarity heuristics.
query_construction: At test time the raw input utterance x_test is encoded by E_X to form the query (no decomposition/expansion). At training-data construction time the candidate set is retrieved using the target output y (using y, i.e. R_u(y, D), found slightly better than using the full pair).
query_granularity: Task-level / instance-level, one-shot at t=0: a single query is formed once per test instance from x_test; no per-step or trajectory-level re-querying.
when_to_retrieve: One-shot: retrieval happens once per test instance before decoding; no iterative or uncertainty-triggered retrieval.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule (retrieve once per test instance, unconditionally, before LM decoding). No confidence/uncertainty/learned-router trigger.
reranking: No dedicated reranking stage at test time; retrieved examples are simply sorted by inner-product similarity. (A two-stage candidate-then-LM-score pipeline exists only during offline training-data construction, not at inference.)
retrieved_context_refinement: None beyond similarity ordering and context-budget truncation: the L most similar examples are sorted high-to-low and the largest prefix L' that fits the context window C is kept; examples are placed in reverse order (lowest-scoring first, highest-scoring nearest to x_test). No decomposition, distillation, compression, or distractor filtering.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tools/skills; demonstrations are raw training examples, not engineered tool/skill descriptions).
index_content_separation: N/A / No: the full demonstration text is what is both indexed (via dense embedding) and loaded into the prompt; no lightweight-index-then-content progressive-disclosure split.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no tool index or live protocol; static FAISS index over a fixed training set).
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (no tools; no inter-tool dependency modeling).
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: retrieved training examples are concatenated (as in-context demonstrations) with the test input and passed as a prefix to the frozen inference LM, which greedily decodes the output. The examples are also a training signal for the retriever itself (LM-scored positives/negatives), but at use-time they are verbatim in-context exemplars.
planning_integration: One-shot exemplars at inference time (retrieve-then-generate). Not interleaved with planning/search; there is a single retrieval call followed by a single greedy decode. No MCTS/tree-search/hierarchical integration.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-answer / per-instance: a single retrieval feeds a single decode of the full output; retrieval is not woven per-CoT-step or per-token.
adaptation_mechanism: Verbatim ICL exemplar: retrieved demonstrations are used as-is in the prompt; there is no explicit case adaptation/revision step (the inference LM may implicitly compose/generalize, analyzed via the 'prompt copying' study, but no algorithmic revision).
retrieved_item_representation: Raw demonstration text: the surface form of each retrieved unit is the concatenation of the training example's input utterance and its gold meaning representation (a raw problem-solution pair), injected directly into the prompt.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Single demonstration (raw, un-distilled training example / problem-solution pair); not a distilled strategy, workflow, or skill.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Retriever-aware training via hard negatives: the contrastive objective uses LM-scored bottom-k candidates (drawn from the same high-similarity BM25 candidate set) as hard negatives plus in-batch negatives, training the retriever to distinguish examples that actually help the LM decode the target from superficially similar but unhelpful ones. No test-time relevance evaluator, self-reflection, or distractor filtering.
memory_type: none (static training-set index; no episodic/skill/workflow memory).
write_back: False: the system does not store new experiences/cases into a memory during deployment; the retrievable store is the fixed offline training set.
online_growth: No: the index is frozen after offline construction; it does not grow at test time.
failure_experience_usage: Not stored as deployment memory, but failure-style signal is used during offline retriever training: bottom-k LM-scored candidates (prompts that lead to LOW probability of the gold output) are used as negative examples in the contrastive objective (success+failure contrastive labeling of the candidate set). No storage/retrieval of test-time failures.
memory_evolution_update: N/A / append-only-none: stored entries are never mutated; the training-set index is fixed.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Partially: the retriever is a learned (contrastively trained) dense scorer rather than a fixed off-the-shelf similarity, but it is NOT an RL/value-based policy. Selection at test time is fixed top-L by learned inner-product similarity (not an MDP/RL policy).
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No: single-model, single private retriever/index. (One cross-model transfer is shown — a retriever trained with a small scoring LM, GPT-Neo, is applied to larger inference LMs GPT-J/GPT-3/Codex — but there is no shared multi-agent memory.)
benchmarks: BREAK (low-level subset; 44K/7K/8K train/dev/test), MTOP (English subset; 16K/2K/4K), SMCALFLOW (15K dev examples, 134K train sampled to 44K). Tasks map utterances to meaning representations (QDMR steps, nested intent-slot queries, and dataflow programs respectively).
benchmark_family: Semantic parsing / structured sequence-to-sequence (utterance-to-meaning-representation). Not in the standard agent/web/embodied/tool benchmark families; closest normalized grouping is QA/structured-parsing (BREAK is a question-understanding/decomposition benchmark; MTOP and SMCALFLOW are task-oriented dialogue semantic parsing).
baselines: Unsupervised: RANDOM, SBERT (paraphrase-mpnet-base-v2), BM25, BRUTEFORCE (test-time LM prompt-selection from Shin et al. 2021). Supervised (same BM25 candidate template, differ in scoring function): DR-BM25 (BM25 scores label positives/negatives), CBR (Case-Based Reasoning, adapted from Das et al. 2021 using token-F1 between outputs). Oracles: BM25-ORACLE (BM25 on gold y_test), LM-ORACLE (LM scoring at test time, upper bound for EPR), ANYCORRECT-ORACLE (any BM25 candidate yields correct output).
key_metrics: Exact-match-style accuracy: LF-EM (logical-form exact match) for BREAK dev; NEM (normalized EM, the official metric) for BREAK test; EM (exact match) for MTOP and SMCALFLOW.
headline_result: When the scoring LM and inference LM are identical (GPT-Neo), EPR improves over the best baseline from 26.0 to 31.9 (LF-EM) on BREAK, from 57.0 to 64.2 (EM) on MTOP, and from 51.4 to 54.3 (EM) on SMCALFLOW (dev set, LM-as-a-service). EPR also outperforms BM25-ORACLE on BREAK and MTOP.
ablations: 1) Hyperparameter robustness (Table 8): varying k in {1,5,10} and candidate-set size L in {50,100} yields stable performance (e.g. BREAK 31.0-32.3, MTOP 63.0-64.2). 2) Unsupervised candidate retriever: BM25 > SBERT, so BM25 is used to build candidate sets. 3) Scoring-LM vs inference-LM mismatch: using GPT-Neo as scoring LM vs GPT-J itself only changes GPT-J BREAK from 31.5 to 33.6; Codex scoring itself 29.5 vs 29.3 — small LM as proxy is effective. 4) One-shot vs full-context (Table 4): EPR 23.0 (one-shot) vs 31.9 (full-context) LF-EM on BREAK; EPR beats BM25-ORACLE one-shot. 5) Prompt-copying analysis (Table 7): higher accuracy on exactly/abstractly copied patterns, but non-negligible accuracy on novel structures (generalization). 6) Cross-LM generalization (Table 5): consistent EPR gains across GPT-3, Codex, GPT-J, GPT-Neo as inference LMs.
evaluation_decoupling: No: only end-to-end downstream task accuracy (LF-EM/EM/NEM) is reported. No separate intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k/nDCG); oracles (LM-ORACLE, ANYCORRECT-ORACLE) bound achievable end-task accuracy rather than measuring retrieval recall directly.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome (final decoded-output exact match). Some process-level analysis is added qualitatively: prompt-copying analysis (exact vs abstract copying, copy-distance distribution) and t-SNE/OPTICS clustering of learned representations, but these are diagnostic, not scored process metrics.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Efficiency is a central motivation: training a light-weight BERT-base dense retriever lets a small scoring LM (GPT-Neo) serve as a cheap proxy for large inference LMs, avoiding expensive per-test-instance LM calls. Test-time retrieval is a single FAISS MIPS lookup (cheap) vs BRUTEFORCE which scores 200 examples with the LM at test time (slow, and worse). No explicit latency/$ numbers reported; training used 8x RTX 3090, batch size 120, lr 1e-4, 30 epochs (DPR defaults).
context_budget_and_selection_count: Budget-capped, dynamic k: maximum inference-LM context C=2,048 tokens. After retrieving the top-L examples sorted by similarity, the largest prefix L' fitting within C (reserving room for x_test and the desired output length) is kept; the number of in-context examples therefore varies per instance (App. Figure 5 shows the distribution). Candidate-set size for training L=50 (also tried 100); k=5 positives/negatives.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (uses existing benchmarks rather than constructing a new one). Datasets used: BREAK (~60K examples low-level subset), MTOP (~22K English subset), SMCALFLOW (~148K, sampled to 44K train + 15K dev).
builds_on: DPR (Karpukhin et al. 2020) contrastive dual-encoder training with in-batch negatives; BERT-base encoders (Devlin et al. 2019); FAISS (Johnson et al. 2017) for indexing; GPT-style in-context learning (Brown et al. 2020 / GPT-3); GPT-Neo (Black et al. 2021) as scoring/inference LM; BM25 (Robertson & Zaragoza 2009) and SBERT (Reimers & Gurevych 2019) as candidate/unsupervised retrievers.
contrasts_with: Liu et al. (2021a) KATE — unsupervised nearest-neighbor (SBERT) prompt selection; Das et al. (2021) CBR — supervised retriever for KB-QA relying on formal-query surface similarity (adapted as the CBR baseline); Shin et al. (2021) BRUTEFORCE — test-time LM prompt selection (slow); plain BM25/SBERT/RANDOM example selection. EPR's distinction: train the retriever from LM-utility labels rather than surface similarity, and do the LM scoring offline rather than at test time.
lineage: Group A (ICL demonstration retrieval). A foundational early (2021/2022) learned dense demonstration retriever: it moves the field from unsupervised similarity-based example selection (KATE) toward LM-feedback-trained retrievers, and is a direct predecessor of later learned/reranking ICL retrievers (e.g. CEIL, UDR, LLM-R, dr.icl) and reward/feedback-trained prompt retrievers.
